newsitem.title: HONDURAS: U.S. unwilling to pay Honduras to keep troops there.
newsitem.headline: U.S. unwilling to pay Honduras to keep troops there.

text.p: The United States is not prepared to pay Honduras for the right to keep troops in the Central American nation, a senior army officer said on Thursday.

"The United States simply does not pay rent for the bases it maintains around the world," Gen. Wesley Clark, commander-in-chief of the U.S. Southern Command, told radio reporters. "We only have bases in places where it serves mutual interests, as is the case here."

The Honduran armed forces have asked the government of President Carlos Roberto Reina to propose that Washington pay $12 million a year in return for the presence of some 500 U.S. soldiers on Honduran soil.

U.S. military personnel have been based at the Palmerola army base, about 35 miles (60 km) north of the capital Tegucigalpa, since 1983, when the leftist Sandinistas governed Nicaragua and civil wars raged in El Salvador and Guatemala.
Honduras in the 1980s was home to one of the biggest CIA operations and the site of annual U.S. army manoeuvres as part of Washington's anti-communist effort in the region.
Reina said in September that the 1954 bilateral treaty allowing the troops' presence should be revised but said no formal approach had been made to the U.S. government.
The Honduran armed forces are struggling to deal with budget cuts and the recent introduction of voluntary rather than compulsory military service.
